new_title: Solheim Cup golf 2026: Europe 4-4 USA after day one drama in fourballs - as it happened
old_text:
One notable conversation point after seeing the fourballs is that all 24 players will have had a hit on the opening day. That has to be good for team morale surely. Then again, will Leona Maguire be smiling through gritted teeth? Her record in this event is phenomenal, now reading 9-3-1 after this morning's win. There was surely a strong argument to send her out again although the line-ups were likely decided some time in advance.
European skipper Anna Nordqvist waves enthusiastically to the crowds surrounding the first tee box. She even does a jig to some folk dressed as bananas. Well, why wouldn't you? Support from fruit is always welcome.
Thanks Scott! Well, what a fascinating morning that was. The first opening session to be tied since 2015 at St. Leon Rot in Germany. That one finished 14.5-13.5 to the USA and it's hard to see this year's edition being anything but tight. Indeed, a number of shrewd judges have even gone for the tie - the outcome that unfolded at Finca Cortesin in Spain in 2023.
The afternoon fourballs have been announced. And they are ...
12.05pm (BST): Charley Hull and Lottie Woad v Yealimi Noh and Angel Yin
12.20pm: Celine Boutier and Nanna Madsen v Megan Khang and Alison Lee
12.35pm: Mimi Rhodes and Nastasia Nadaud v Allisen Corpuz and Auston Kim
12.50pm: Carlota Ciganda and Julia Lopez Ramirez v Nelly Korda and Lauren Coughlin
Something of a surprise that Boutier and Madsen have been given another run-out, because neither player was anywhere near their best this morning. A good chance to right some wrongs, though. Penny for the thoughts of Leona Maguire, who it's safe to say usually doesn't care too much for being stood down.
Your friend and mine, David Tindall will take you through the afternoon action. Enjoy, enjoy, and I'll see you all again tomorrow morning.
That was a fantastic morning of matchplay golf. Allisen Corpuz and Nelly Korda made Solheim Cup history by becoming the first pairing to post a five-and-zero record in foursomes. They were magnificent, but then so was Lottie Woad, who made several crucial putts to keep the score semi-respectable. Leona Maguire, Maja Stark and Linn Grant did their usual thing for Europe, too. This is lining up to be one hell of a weekend. Incidentally, the USA had the honour this morning, hence the ordering of the scores, but allow me to cock a snook to consistency and switch everything around as we go into the rest of the tournament. So sue me!*
Hull/Woad v Corpuz/Korda 4&3
Madsen/Boutier v Al. Lee/Coughlin 3&2
2UP Henseleit/Maguire v An. Lee/Duncan
3&2 Stark/Grant v Zhang/Kupcho Europe 2-2 USA
Lee sets her putt rolling serenely towards the hole. It's surely going in ... but somehow it drifts to the right on its final turn and misses by the width of a dimple. Team USA pick up Leona Maguire's coin - she's got two putts from as many feet - and Europe win the match 2UP. Esther Henseleit and Leona Maguire beat Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan 2UP
Henseleit sends a crisp wedge flying towards the flagstick. Too fierce? Not a bit of it! The ball grips and spins, before rolling out to three feet. That's a wonderful shot under pressure, and now Andrea Lee has to make the par putt if the USA are to realistically snatch half a point. But if there's anyone the USA would pick to take this putt, it's surely Lee ...
Lindy Duncan steps up to the plate. A wedge over the flag that lands 20 feet past before spinning back to ten. A chance for par. Over to Esther Henseleit, just off the front of the green ...
Leona Maguire up first. She creams a hybrid and gives it a twirl, though the ball doesn't reach the green, rolling to a halt a few yards short. Andrea Lee meanwhile hits a slightly heavy shot out of the bunker, the ball toying with the creek running across the middle of the fairway. But it gets over. The US pair are about 80 yards out, so an up and down for par is far from a pipe dream, and would put all sorts of pressure on the European duo.
... she sends her tee shot to the right again, just as she did on 16. But not so far that it goes into the bunker that (reportedly - the cameras haven't shown it) snaffled Duncan's ball. So it's advantage Europe. Many hard yards to travel yet, though.
Lindy Duncan sends her tee shot into a bunker down the right of the 18th fairway. A world of possibilities opens up for Europe ... but Esther Henseleit sent her last tee shot into the drink, so the nerves will be jangling. And ...
Esther Henseleit rolls in the par saver! She fist-pumps the air and Europe are dormie. Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan will have to win 18 if the USA are to go into the afternoon fourballs with an advantage.
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 1UP (17)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 3&2 (F)
Europe's ball on 17 is behind a hillock to the right of the green. Leona Maguire doesn't have much room to work with, but she lands a graceful chip onto the far side of the bank, her ball rolling out to four feet. Andrea Lee's long birdie putt stops just short of the hole, so Esther Henseleit will have the opportunity to make amends for her recent errors. But it's no gimme ...
... Rose Zhang holes her 15-foot right-to-left swinger! Europe have two putts for the win ... and Maja Stark leaves a tentative dribbler a couple of feet short and wide left! Work to do ... but Linn Grant completes the job. Europe on the board! Maja Stark and Linn Grant beat Rose Zhang and Jennifer Kupcho 3&2
Europe might be denied in this last match, though. Esther Henseleit, a little shaken perhaps by the mistake on the 16th tee, sends her approach at 17 towards trouble to the right of the green. Lindy Duncan finds the putting surface in regulation. So this could be all square again soon. Then on 16 ...
Linn Grant sends her wedge over the flag on 16, the ball spinning to a halt 15 feet past. Then it's Jennifer Kupcho from the dropzone, which in a quirky twist is located further out than Grant's ball. Kupcho gets a little bit closer than Grant, but only a gut-punching twist would deny Europe now.
Better news for Europe in the anchor match. Rose Zhang decides to go for the 16th green in two. She's got little option but to roll the dice, because the USA are dormie three. And she doesn't catch her fairway wood properly, sending the ball scampering apologetically into the creek guarding the front of the green. Maja Stark lays up in front of the water, and Europe are closing in on their first point of the week.
... and Europe's quest for parity doesn't begin well, as Team USA snatch a hole back in match three. Esther Henseleit's errant drive proving costly in the end.
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 1UP (16)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 3UP (15)
Europe still have an extremely good chance of salvaging parity from this morning session. But there's plenty of work to be done to close out the last two matches, and if they somehow let things slip, it'll be pretty dispiriting for the hosts.
3&2 Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (F)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (15)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 3UP (15)
... but she can't do it. Madsen tugs a nervous effort wide left, never dropping, and it's a 3&2 victory for the USA! Anything other than an American win would have been an affront, really, if we're being totally honest with ourselves, because both Madsen and Boutier were way off their A-games. Alison Lee and Lauren Coughlin beat Nanna Koertz Madsen and Celine Boutier 3&2
Celine Boutier leaves Europe's long birdie putt on 16 four feet short. It had been bang on line, but she simply didn't hit it. That gives Alison Lee the chance to win the match, which she nearly does, a big right-to-left swinger stopping a couple of inches short. So now Nanna Madsen has to make a missable putt to keep the match alive ...
Jennifer Kupcho wedges to six feet from the dropzone at 15. But that still leaves Linn Grant with two putts for the win, and she cradles her effort to tap-in distance. The hole is conceded and Europe are dormie three in the anchor match.
2UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (15)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (15)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 3UP (15)
More aquatic shenanigans. Esther Henseleit carves her drive at 16 into Boutier's Creek. Hanging around for that ruling won't have helped her there. Lindy Duncan dry. Meanwhile up the hole, Lauren Coughlin and Nanna Madsen find the green with their third shots. Neither particularly close. The USA will be much happier about that, given their 2UP advantage.
Back on the par-three 15th, yet another player dunks their tee shot into the lake to the left of the green! Rose Zhang the culprit this time. Maja Stark doesn't make the mistake Celine Boutier did earlier, following up by aiming for the heart of the green. Safe and dry. Huge advantage to Europe, who can almost touch dormie three in the anchor match.
A big break for Europe. The referee decides the bridge is in Boutier's road, so she'll get relief. A drop, no closer to the pin, but still in the hazard. So she's able to go from the right side of the bank to the left, closer to the fairway. And because any dropped ball would roll into the creek, she can place. She whips back into the fairway, and Europe are alive and kicking. Just.
Europe's ball is dry. But it's in the hazard. Boutier wants a line-of-sight ruling, with a spectator bridge ahead of her. However that's not the route she'd be taking with her next shot, back onto the fairway, so the referee's not having it. Not immediately, anyway. After some back and forth, it looks like Boutier will get her drop, but there's going to be some more discussion. In the meantime, the putting contest on 15 is halved and the teams move on.
2UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (15)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (15)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 2UP (14)
The rain continues to pelt down. As if it wasn't wet enough, Nanna Madsen sends her tee shot dangerously close to the creek running down the right of 16. The camera loses the ball, so more on that when we have it. Meanwhile back on 15, both Leona Maguire and Andrea Lee find the depression in the middle of the green, short of the flag on the wrong level. And Maja Stark makes a missable six-footer on 14 for the half. Everything oscillating in the breeze at the moment, with all these matches on knife-edges.
2UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (15)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (14)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 2UP (14)
Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan zig-zag their way up 14 like the Keystone Kops. They end up with double bogey, and should probably concede the hole, but allow Leona Maguire the opportunity to make her par putt and get the crowd going. And there are more roars on 15, where Alison Lee leaves her bogey putt short, opening the door again for Europe. Celine Boutier barrels through it by making the putt, and making up for her mistake from the tee. Europe still alive!
2UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (15)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (14)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 2UP (13)
To the drop zone! And onto the green from 100 yards. Nanna Madsen gets closer than Lauren Coughlin, the latter ending up at the bottom of a bowl in front of the pin, the former pin high on the correct shelf. There's quite a bit of break on the USA putt, over a ridge, while the European chance is straighter and flatter. Big putting contest coming up!
It's started raining quite heavily at Bernardus. Alison Lee takes some time to towel down her grip before taking her tee shot at the par-three 15th ... then sends her ball into the drink! The door suddenly open for Europe ... but then Celine Boutier follows her in! Boutier's jaw nearly hits the floor. She went for the pin, bringing the water on the left into play, when the match situation demanded a safe route into the heart of the green. What a brain freeze. A huge chance to get back into the match spurned.
3UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (14)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 1UP (13)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 2UP (13)
Andrea Lee skelps a long-range birdie putt into the hole on 13. That almost slam-dunked into the cup, such was the speed it was travelling. Had it not hit the hole, the ball may have ended up in Belgium. Meanwhile on 14, Nanna Madsen makes up for her wild drive by nearly holing out from the heather to scramble a half. Dormie four avoided, but Europe are still on the brink.
4&3 Corpuz/Korda v Hull/Woad (F)
3UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (14)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 1UP (13)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 2UP (13)
Charley Hull has to get aggressive with her putt on 15. She's got to make birdie. Her effort sails miles past. Nelly Korda's 20-footer lips out to a couple of feet. Lottie Woad has to make the par putt if she's to have any chance of keeping Europe alive ... and in it goes! She's now rammed in four putts on this back nine! And yet it's all been in vain. Allisen Corpuz tidies up for the half, and the USA win 4&3. Corpuz and Korda five-and-zero in this format! Allisen Corpuz and Nelly Korda beat Charley Hull and Lottie Woad 4&3
Lottie Woad and Allisen Corpuz both find the green at the par-three 15th. But Corpuz is closer, and so the first point of the day is within touching distance for Team USA now.
Nanna Madsen is put off by a rendition of the Viking Roar that soundtracked Norway's World Cup campaign. Does a Dane need to hear that? Either way, she flays her drive at 14 into rubbish down the right. Europe have struggled badly in this second match, and dormie four looms.
4UP Corpuz/Korda v Hull/Woad (14)
3UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (13)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (12)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 2UP (12)
Charley Hull makes the birdie putt, and Europe stay alive in the lead match! It ain't over 'til it's over.
4UP Corpuz/Korda v Hull/Woad (14)
3UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (13)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (12)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 2UP (11)
All is almost lost in the lead match, but Lottie Woad is not giving up without a fight. She responds to Allisen Corpuz coming up short of the green with her approach by sticking her second pin high to six feet. But Nelly Korda chips up to three feet, so Charley Hull will have to make the putt to extend. Meanwhile in match two, the USA go three up despite Alison Lee racing a birdie putt four feet past. Lauren Coughlin tidies up to take control of that one.
Andrea Lee does what Andrea Lee does so often. A 12-footer to save the half on 12. That's a huge moment for the USA in match three, because Esther Henseleit had an opportunity to make birdie from similar distance just before.
5UP Corpuz/Korda v Hull/Woad (13)
2UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (12)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (12)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 2UP (11)
... but Korda isn't missing from three feet. The USA go 5UP with five to play in the lead match. Europe teetering. And suddenly things are going in the wrong direction for the hosts in the anchor match, Jennifer Kupcho winning a putting contest with Linn Grant on 11 to win a second hole in a matter of minutes. Europe's lead in that one sliced in half, quicksmart.
5UP Corpuz/Korda v Hull/Woad (13)
2UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (12)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (11)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 2UP (11)
Scrub that about dormie five? Lottie Woad makes another big putt, securing bogey and forcing Nelly Korda to make the USA's par putt! That's a third huge putt by Woad in four holes ...
Nelly Korda sends her second into 13 over the back-right of the green. The door's open for Europe ... but Charley Hull follows Korda down there. Then after Allisen Corpuz bundles her chip up to three feet, Lottie Woad underhits her effort, the ball only just making the green before toppling back down the swale. Hull gives the putt up a good rap, but that flies ten feet past, and in a minute or so, the USA will be dormie five in the lead match.
Maja Stark can't make a birdie putt on 10. Their opponents are on the par-five green in two, and close, so the hole's conceded. Up on 11, Leona Maguire sends a dart at the flag, and Esther Henseleit tidies up for birdie and a two-hole advantage. And on 12, Nanna Madsen holes a tramliner from downtown to scramble a half. Alison Lee had sent her second very close, so that was some act of escapology.
4UP Corpuz/Korda v Hull/Woad (12)
2UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (12)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 2UP (11)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 3UP (10)
Celine Boutier makes the awkward par putt on 11 to scramble a half. Even better for Europe: Maja Stark leaves Linn Grant in a bunker greenside at 9, only for Grant to hole out for par. Rose Zhang's birdie putt suddenly looks a lot longer than it did, and dies away on the low side. Another half scrambled for Europe, and that's one heck of a momentum-saver. But the inevitable happens on 12 after Lottie Woad's visit to the water. Allisen Corpuz and Nelly Korda closing in on becoming the first pairing in Solheim Cup history to enjoy a five-and-zero winning record in this discipline.
4UP Corpuz/Korda v Hull/Woad (12)
2UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (11)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 1UP (9)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 4UP (9)
Nanna Madsen gets super-aggressive with a putt from the fringe on 11. Her ball rolls 12 feet past. This match is getting away from Europe. See also the lead match, where Charley Hull sends Europe's tee shot into the heather down the right of 12. Lottie Woad can't get good contact on the ball, hitting it heavy and dunking it into a creek short of the green.
Lauren Coughlin walks in the eagle putt on 10 to double USA's lead in match two. Esther Henseleit misses a short putt on 9 to gift a hole to the USA. And in the lead match, both teams get up and down from the side of the green, but once again it's Lottie Woad grinding it out, rolling in a staunch six-footer to halve the hole. Without those two big putts on 10 and 11, Europe would be in a world of pain. Woad may be 3DOWN but she's been mighty impressive on debut.
3UP Corpuz/Korda v Hull/Woad (11)
2UP Coughlin/Al. Lee v Koerstz Madsen/Boutier (10)
An. Lee/Duncan v Henseleit/Maguire 1UP (9)
Zhang/Kupcho v Stark/Grant 4UP (8)
new_text:
Carlota Ciganda hasn't had a top 30 finish since May and she's missed the cut in the year's last four majors. But put her in a Solheim Cup environment and everything changes. The Spaniard, who has now won 13 matches in her Solheim career, had this to say.
"I love this week. I love playing for the team, for my team-mates, for Anna Nordqvist; she is a good friend. I want to win for her.
"I think not losing today is important. That's big momentum going into tomorrow and hopefully we can win both morning and afternoon.
"I would love to keep playing with Julia Lopez Ramirez, but whatever the captain wants us to do, we will do it."
Day two is the same format as Thursday. That means 4 x morning foursomes followed by 4 x fourballs in the afternoon. It's all rounded off with Sunday's singles.
Well, what a finish. Incredible putts by Ciganda at 16 and 18 to secure the tie. Both sessions shared 2-2 highlights just how balanced these two teams are.
Hull/Woad v Noh/Yin Tied
Madsen/Boutier v Khang/Lee 4&3
2&1 Rhodes/Nadaud v Corpuz/Kim
Ciganda/Lopez Ramirez A/S Korda/Coughlin Tied
... Korda's putt comes up short but she may have given her playing partner a read. Coughlin doesn't hit it either! It was in the heart! You can't leave that short! Europe still alive. Over to you Carlota!
The drone shot shows that there's a very clear opening for Ciganda. She flicks up her wedge to about 20 feet away so, if Korda and Coughlin can't convert, the Spaniard could add another tale to her Solheim Cup story.
... Korda turns the screw and hits a fine approach to not just par range but very realistic birdie range. Coughlin gives that screw another twist by hitting her second a fraction inside her playing partner's ball.
Does Ciganda have any sort of shot here? She's actually on the 1st fairway. Sophie Walker, out on the course, reckons 'it's on' so you never know.
Ciganda recalling Jordan Spieth at Birkdale in 2017 here. It's a blind second over an obstacle (in this case, a tree). There's water around the green though and she'll likely have to fly it 180 yards to avoid the wet stuff and sand so the degree of difficulty is high. She pulls 4-iron but catches it heavy and it's way right of the green. Hard to see how she makes par now. Lopez Ramirez has a good lie in the bunker but hits it fat and smashes into the lip. The ball drops apologetically back into sand. Here third comes up short of the green. Europe making a mess of this 18th.
The sun shines straight into the players' eyes as they tee off at 18. Lopez Ramirez wants her ball to draw but it doesn't listen and finds sand. Ciganda hits it way right but her ball actually settles on short grass. She'll have to hit over a tree with her second though.
No such trouble for Korda who launches a 3-wood down the middle of the fairway. Coughlin follows suit so advantage USA here.
Hull/Woad v Noh/Yin Tied
Madsen/Boutier v Khang/Lee 4&3
2&1 Rhodes/Nadaud v Corpuz/Kim
Ciganda/Lopez Ramirez A/S Korda/Coughlin (17)
... Coughlin goes first and does enough to secure a par. As the sun sets, Lopez Ramirez is next and that's also good for a four. Korda and Ciganda are equidistant so the ref has to come in and make a call. Korda putts first but it's always on the high side. Can Ciganda pull out some magic again? She stalks her left-to-righter from 20 feet and it has a chance but not this time. The Spaniard drops to her knees in frustration. Actually, Europe make the USA putt which is no problem for Coughlin. To 18...
Back to 17 and can either side grab a lead and go dormie? Ciganda's know-how could be vital here and she plonks a 9-iron to perhaps 20 feet. Korda, Coughlin and Lopez Ramirez will also have looks at birdie, the latter two of the outside variety.
Up to the 17th green where Europe are on the cusp of victory. Auston Kim has a 15-footer to keep the Americans alive but she misses left. Another point on the board for Europe and a superb effort by the rookies Mimi Rhodes and Nastasia Nadaud. The match is tied! Mimi Rhodes and Nastasia Nadaud beat Allisen Corpuz and Auston Kim 2&1
Carlota Ciganda shows all her vast Solheim Cup experience by holing a 20 footer for eagle at 16. The bottom match is all square again! 'Vamos' she roars as the putt catches enough of the left side of the cup to do a Jose Maria Olazabal-style jig and drop.
Hull/Woad v Noh/Yin Tied
Madsen/Boutier v Khang/Lee 4&3
2UP Rhodes/Nadaud v Corpuz/Kim (16)
Ciganda/Lopez Ramirez A/S Korda/Coughlin (16)
Rhodes and Nadaud have now gone dormie over Corpuz and Kim in Match 3. But the Europeans will want to finish it off either on 17 or 18 after halving 16 in par fives.
Huge moments these now. A sense that things are turning the way of the Americans. Woad is first to putt from about 25 feet at 18. Some daft background music is putting Woad off and she backs away. Finally Woad settles over her putt which is nicely struck but just stays left. Now for Noh as the music keeps pumping. Turn the bloody thing off! Noh is perhaps distracted too and it's never on line. The top game is halved. A great fightback and full credit to Noh for inspiring the revival, virtually on her own. Charley Hull and Lottie Woad halved with Yealimi Noh and Angel Yin
Back to 18. Yin and Hull aren't in the hole so it's down to Woad v Noh. Woad pulls her approach left of the flag to around 25 feet while Noh, shielding her eyes from the setting sun after hitting a smooth short iron, will have about half that.
Carlota Ciganda's birdie putt at 15 looks to be turning towards the hole but just pulls up short. Agony for the Spaniard. It leaves the door open for Korda but her putt deviates left at the death so on they go to the 16th with the USA still 1up in the pivotal bottom match.
Hull/Woad A/S Noh/Yin (17)
Madsen/Boutier v Khang/Lee 4&3
2UP Rhodes/Nadaud v Corpuz/Kim (15)
Ciganda/Lopez Ramirez v Korda/Coughlin 1UP (15)
To the 18th. Noh stripes her tee-shot down the middle while Yin looks to have found sand. Huge pressure on Woad and Hull now as they stare down the barrel of letting a serious lead slip and suffering a second defeat of the day.
Woad stays strong and finds the fairway but Hull looks to have tugged her drive into a hazard down the left.
At 17, Hull has the pace but not the line with her birdie putt. Woad, also from around 20 feet, doesn't give it enough so Noh has a putt to tie the match. She lines it up and ... never in doubt. A superb birdie when it mattered most. Noh has been brilliant on this back nine.
Back at 14, Ciganda and Lopez Ramirez get away with a halve so stay just 1 down.
Hull/Woad A/S Noh/Yin (17)
Madsen/Boutier v Khang/Lee 4&3
2UP Rhodes/Nadaud v Corpuz/Kim (15)
Ciganda/Lopez Ramirez v Korda/Coughlin 1UP (14)
Another sensational shot from Noh. The fairway bunker she's in at 17 has a high lip and clearing it shouldn't be taken for granted. But she not only makes great connection, her ball arrows towards the flag, almost shakes hands with it, and pulls back to around six feet. Woad and Hull are much further away so this top match is far from over.
It's a win for Corpuz and Kim at 15 so they cut the lead of Rhodes and Nadaud to 2up.
1UP Hull/Woad v Noh/Yin (16)
Madsen/Boutier v Khang/Lee 4&3
2UP Rhodes/Nadaud v Corpuz/Kim (15)
Ciganda/Lopez Ramirez v Korda/Coughlin 1UP (13)
Shot of the day contender from Allisen Corpuz. With Europe 3up at 15, the Americans need something special and Corpuz starts the process by hitting her tee shot to within two feet of the flag at the par 3. A guaranteed birdie.
Noh's tee-shot at 17 heads left and ... is gobbled up by a bunker. Yin finds the rough/heather so she's not in great position either. No such problem for Woad who splits the fairway while Hull's drive kicks back onto the short grass. Europe in great position there now.
... from just over 15 feet, Woad's eagle putt catches a piece of the hole but not enough. The US putt is conceded - "rather generous, I would say", according to Catriona Matthew in the commentary box - so Woad and Hull stay 1up with two to play.
1UP Hull/Woad v Noh/Yin (16)
Madsen/Boutier v Khang/Lee 4&3
3UP Rhodes/Nadaud v Corpuz/Kim (14)
Ciganda/Lopez Ramirez v Korda/Coughlin 1UP (13)
Under darkening skies at the par-5 16th, Lottie Woad lights up the greenside crowd with a wonderful second shot to set up an eagle. Hull's delightful chip to secure a birdie means Woad will have a free run at it.
Ciganda and Lopez Ramirez, who three-putts, can't find a par at 13 and that means Coughlin and the rather subdued World No.1 Korda go 1up again.
1UP Hull/Woad v Noh/Yin (15)
Madsen/Boutier v Khang/Lee 4&3
3UP Rhodes/Nadaud v Corpuz/Kim (13)
Ciganda/Lopez Ramirez v Korda/Coughlin 1UP (13)
Europe need to birdie the par-3 15th to stay alive after Lee hits a glorious tee shot. It's not to be and Lee and Khang score a dominant 4&3 win over Boutier and Madsen, who suffer their second defeat of the day. USA lead the Solheim Cup 3-2. Megan Khang and Alison Lee beat Celine Boutier and Nanna Koerstz Madsen 4&3
A whoop from Mimi Rhodes as she holes from 15 feet for a winning birdie at 13. She and fellow rookie Nastasia Nadaud have roared into a 3up lead after 13 with a burst of three wins in four holes. Matches 2 and 3 look set to be split 1-1 which means everything is hanging on those top and bottom matches.
1UP Hull/Woad v Noh/Yin (15)
